primary: Exploration primary: all externally arrived requests mean completion flow; failures and unfinished cannot be omitted or treated as success. Complete output rate, TTFT, per-request maximum generation gaps, final drain and individual harms are required side effects. Tradeoffs allowed; no post-hoc SLO or significance claim.
slo: No application SLO. Inherited20point frontier is diagnostic only.
hypothesis: Under equal immediate physical release and equal computed whole pages, retaining requests with a smaller declared remaining output budget may complete them earlier and sustain capacity relief. Native re-admission and extra recovery of the longer displaced request may instead absorb or reverse that effect.
claim_ceiling: One exploratory ABBA of a complete online simple remaining-budget baseline. This is a bounded diagnostic component adaptation related to shortest-remaining-work scheduling, not a new method or full CacheOPT reproduction. No exact EOS prediction, strict same-hidden-state causal effect, independent confirmation, equal work/quality or novel contribution is assumed.
retention: All cells and failures retained; at most this one ABBA. No threshold, trigger-position, sharing, arrival or capacity scans. Zero action permits only a bounded entry/opportunity diagnosis; no repeated same-domain search.
capacity_source: Explicit same physical KV-byte budget from completed normal .90 profile on this exact GPU. Prior profile prefix enabled, present original mixed workload prefix disabled; only that engine flag differs intentionally. Not a fresh prefix-off normal profile and not an old-device timing baseline.
simple_comparators: Native tail is the executed control; equal-release-budget is the strong simple baseline under test. Existing first-output-equivalent protection and host-prefix probes did not support stable mean-flow benefit. Max actual-release stays shadow here and remains an unexecuted competing baseline. No claim of beating tuned nearest systems.

diagnostic_question: Does complete online equal-capacity remaining-budget victim ordering reduce all-arrival mean completion flow by allowing retained requests to finish, after including longer displaced victims and native re-admission?
decision_rule: Zero actual choices: inspect recorded opportunity/guards, do not expand. Executed choices without mean-flow support or with loss transfer: close this formulation in this domain without threshold/workload searches. Uncertain within the one-group cap: report unresolved, no automatic repeat. Supported mean-flow benefit: first credit the simple baseline and examine residual loss and nearest comparator; no added-signal novelty. Throughput/TTFT/gaps/per-request harms are disclosed tradeoffs, not a requirement that every metric improve.

runtime_scope: Only native allocation-failure victim selection differs. Every decision re-evaluates the legal unprocessed suffix. Tail and alternative are private qualified RUNNING pure-decode with outputs>0 and pending STORE=0, and have equal immediate releasable blocks and floor(computed/block_size). Select the maximum declared max_tokens-output_tokens, latest index on ties, replace only when strictly larger than tail. Unknown physical/progress/budget/pending metadata or active protection/phase returns tail. Host state does not rank or qualify. Other native scheduling, preempt/free, Q1/target/1s trigger/quantum/transfer/admission and all observations are identical.
